newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Exchange sets rules for derivatives warrants.
newsitem.headline: HK Exchange sets rules for derivatives warrants.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said it would introduce a qualifying period with immediate effect on the criteria for issuing single share derivative warrants or basket warrants.
The exchange said the underlying share in respect of single share derivative warrants must have a public float capitalisation of at least HK$4 billion.

Each underlying share in basket warrants must have either a public float capitalisation of at least HK$4 billion or be subject to the weighting requirements set out in the listing rules of a public float capitalisation of HK$1 billion, it said.

The exchange said it would not consider a share as having satisfied the public float requirements, if, on any business day during the period of 90 days immediately preceding the intended date of launch of the relevant derivative warrants, the public float capitalisation of that share was:

a) less than HK$4 billion in respect of single share derivative, or b) less than HK$4 billion in respect of basket warrants where the share is not to be subject to the weighting requirements set out in listing rule, or
c) less than HK$1 billion in respect of basket warrants where the share is to be subject to the weighting requirements.

The Exchange also said it would retain the discretion to allow the listing of derivative warrants relating to shares listed on an overseas exchange, the market capitalisation of the share is at least HK$10 billion.

It said it would not consider a share as having satisfied the market capitalisation requirement if on any business day during the period of 90 days immediately preceding the intended date of launch of the relevant derivative warrants, the market capitalisation of that share was less than HK$10 billion.
